content.text:
I've submitted index 15 (Mn 0.51 / Y 0.49) as the best composition. It gave the highest photocurrent of the three I measured, 5.8e-7 A. That is only the best of the samples I tested. I measured 3 of the 26 compositions, so a better one may exist among those not tested.

| Index | Mn : Y | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 15 | 0.51 : 0.49 | **5.8e-7 A** |
| 10 | 0.42 : 0.58 | 5e-8 A |
| 14 | 0.66 : 0.34 | −9e-8 A |

- **Picking the first two:** I tested index 15 because it sits next to the 1:1 compound YMnO3, which is listed in the Materials Project data. I tested index 14 because it sits next to a 2:1 compound, YMn₂O₅. Index 14 gave essentially no photocurrent.
- **Picking the third:** the model that suggests the next measurement (a Gaussian process) chose index 10. It came out more than ten times lower than index 15. Since the photocurrent fell on both sides, the best composition is probably close to 1:1. Index 12 (Mn 0.45) or 18 (Mn 0.48) might have beaten index 15.
- **Unused budget:** I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements, so which crystal phases are actually present was never confirmed.
